display.purpose: The H1 only: Hanken Grotesk at 750, −0.025em, 38px below 1024px easing to 56px at 1280px.

section-sm.purpose: Section headings below 640px; also the plan price under 380px.

h3.purpose: Plan names, the result card's headline, display voice.

h4.purpose: Row labels in an opened ledger, the sheet's section labels: 600 at normal tracking.

key-figure.purpose: The surface's one largest number: the Offer Ceiling on the highlight stroke, 54px, display voice with tabular numerals.

key-figure-sm.purpose: The key figure below 1024px, plan prices, the readout's figures on wide screens.

figure.purpose: Every number compared with another or able to change: tabular numerals in the text face at 600 (the Figure rule). Animated through AnimatedNumber.

text.purpose: Marketing body at 18px: the hero subhead (46ch), section intros and notes (60-68ch).

ui.purpose: Fields, nav links, captions, links in running text; 16px so iOS never zooms a field.

label.purpose: Column heads, chips, terms in a ruled list: 14px at 600, sentence case.

small.purpose: Target lines, notes, the risk line, the footer strip.

meta.purpose: Geist Mono at 12-14px, 500: source chips, the sheet's caption row, dimension labels, code. Never figures, never headings.

shadows.name: rest
shadows.purpose: shadow-sm: a card, a plan card or a result card at rest; a hairline and a soft cobalt-tinted shadow 12px below. shadow-xs and shadow-2xs are the hairline alone.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: shadow-md: menus, popovers, tooltips, dialogs, the sticky bars, a hovered plan card.

shadows.name: float-up
shadows.purpose: The float cast upward (shadow-float-up) for bars fixed to the bottom edge.

shadows.name: panel
shadows.purpose: shadow-lg: the hero sheet, a dark instrument panel, the scroll story's pinned frame.

focus.name: control
focus.purpose: Every link, button, field, summary and tabbable element. A floor over the primitives' own rings.

focus.name: menu-item
focus.purpose: Menu items and listbox options, where an outline would sit outside the menu.

motion.name: fast
motion.purpose: State changes: hover, pressed, a chip flipping. Named properties only, never transition: all.

motion.name: base
motion.purpose: A reveal, a float opening, a plan card lifting.

motion.name: slow
motion.purpose: A section's content easing in as it enters the viewport (Reveal, Stagger at 60ms steps).

motion.name: draw
motion.purpose: A line drawing: a leader into the result, the rule under a key figure.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: A figure or the price handle settling on its value: mass and damping, no bounce past the target.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Button press feedback; the link variant does not scale.

motion.name: reduced
motion.value: animation-duration and transition-duration 0.001ms !important under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce; MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"; NumberFlow respects the preference
motion.purpose: Reduced motion shows the end state everywhere, floats included.

narrative.overview:
A rental deal is a drawing before it is a decision: rent flows in, the mortgage and the taxes flow out, and what lands at the bottom is the cash flow. TrueCap draws that on a drafting sheet, annotates every line with where its number came from, and lets the visitor move the price and watch the drawing answer. That object, the deal drawn and alive, is the site's signature.

The sheet, not the spreadsheet. The world is the architect's sheet and the engineer's annotated drawing: a fine grid, graphite lines, leaders and dimension lines, one highlighter stroke on the number that matters. It is not the ledger and not the generic SaaS page.

Scene, and why light. An agent reads it on a phone at a showing, in daylight; the client reads the memo at a desk. So the sheet is light by default, and dark appears as bands and instrument panels, the sheet inverted, never as a theme.

Alive, not decorated. Engagement comes from the product doing something in front of the visitor: a price that drags, figures that roll to their new value, a line that draws to show where a number came from.
keyCharacteristics: A drafting sheet: the faint cobalt grid, graphite lines, leaders and dimension lines, one highlighter stroke under the Offer Ceiling.
One face, Hanken Grotesk, for display (750) and text (400), with tabular numerals for every figure; Geist Mono for metadata only.
Cobalt is the one action color; green and red are the direction of a flow or a pass and a miss; the warm highlight belongs to the Offer Ceiling.
White cards and panels float on the sheet with three elevation steps; dark bands are the sheet inverted.
Light by default, built so a dark theme is possible later; no toggle.
Motion with mass: one library, one spring, transform and opacity only, the resting state is the complete page, reduced motion wins.

rules.name: The Figure rule
rules.body: A number that will be compared with another, or that can change, is set in the text face with tabular numerals (font-figure); a changing figure animates through AnimatedNumber. Never a mono figure.

rules.name: Sentence case everywhere
rules.body: Table heads included. Acronyms stay acronyms (DSCR, NOI, CoC, HUD, FRED). No uppercase tracked micro-labels.

rules.name: One action color
rules.body: Cobalt is the only color that means act here: buttons, links, focus rings, the active nav item, the grid, the dimension line, the handle's border.

rules.name: One warm stroke
rules.body: The highlight is a fill under the Offer Ceiling and the meets-range on the price track; it never carries small text. Its text step marks a miss.

rules.name: The Sign rule
rules.body: Green and red are earned by the direction of a flow or a pass against a target, never for emphasis.

rules.name: Light by default, dark as bands
rules.body: The sheet is the page; navy appears as bands and instrument panels, the sheet inverted. Tokens allow a dark theme later; no toggle ships.

rules.name: Radius by role
rules.body: 4px tags and chips, 8px controls, 12px objects, 14-16px floats; full round for switch tracks, avatars, the price handle and status dots; rules and tables have none.

rules.name: Three elevation steps
rules.body: Rest for cards, float for menus and bars, panel for the hero sheet and dark instruments. Every shadow has an offset and a soft blur; no colored halo, no hard offset. Every float keeps a 1px line under its shadow.

rules.name: Motion with mass
rules.body: One library through MotionProvider, NumberFlow for figures, CSS scroll timelines behind @supports and no-preference. Transform and opacity only; the resting state is the complete page; nothing above the fold starts hidden and the H1 never animates; one authored moment per surface; figures announce on release; reduced motion shows the end state.

rules.name: No eyebrows, no arrows
rules.body: No label, kicker or pill above a heading. Link text never ends in an arrow; buttons carry no trailing arrow icon; nothing nudges sideways on hover.

rules.name: Cards for objects, lines for lists
rules.body: A card is for something the visitor compares or acts on: a plan, a result, a saved deal. Lists, sources and FAQs sit on lines inside their object.

rules.name: Focus
rules.body: A 3px cobalt outline with a 2px offset on every control; menu items and listbox options show the band plus an inset 2px cobalt ring. Controls are at least 44×44px.

dos: Do take every color, radius, shadow, duration and font from tokens.
Do set every figure in font-figure and every changing figure through AnimatedNumber.
Do give every interactive demo a keyboard path and a static end state.
Do keep one Disclaimer per marketing page.
Do keep controls at 44px or more with the 3px ring.
Do keep text-base on inputs below md.
Do use next/image with intrinsic sizes.
donts: Don't add a theme toggle, a second accent, gradient text, a glow, an eyebrow, an arrow suffix, an uppercase label, a mono figure, a card around a list, a colored halo, transition-all, an entrance on the LCP element, or a second animation library.
